title: Veil and Garden
premise: Lior Oyelaran, a mercenary bound to the silent god Veth, keeps accounts for the Gilded Ledger, a guild trading in impossible things—bottled grief, borrowed years, names not yet spoken. When their own name surfaces in a century-old book of prophecies tied to tonight's date, Lior learns they were sold as an infant to the court beneath the mountain, and that the last dragon's dying fire is the only thing keeping that court's stolen souls imprisoned. To survive the prophecy, Lior must steal back their own soul with the help of a disgraced archivist, a dragon-keeper's daughter, and the guild family they never trusted themselves to have. In the end, Lior chooses to shatter the ledger rather than claim their inheritance, freeing every soul—including their own—and answering the silent god at last.
about_author: Ivo Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing guild ledgers in port cities before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about paperwork, gods, and the families we assemble from strangers.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. A night of routine trades at the Gilded Ledger: bottled grief, a borrowed year, a name sold twice. Establishes Lior's meticulous invisibility and their quiet prayers to the god Veth, who has not answered in nine years. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as competence.

chapters.title: Tonight, By Name
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. An archivist named Sefa arrives to authenticate a prophetic codex written a century ago; Lior finds their own full name inscribed under tonight's date. Emotional beat: the floor drops out of a carefully ordered life.

chapters.title: What the Guild Owes
chapters.summary: Guildmaster Ombre's POV. The guildmaster reads the prophecy page and goes pale, revealing she has known about Lior's entry for years. Emotional beat: betrayal braided with protectiveness.

chapters.title: Sold at the Well Gate
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa traces the codex's provenance and finds a bill of sale: an infant named Lior Oyelaran, sold to the Court Beneath the Mountain for one impossible thing. Emotional beat: horror at discovering a person was ever currency.

chapters.title: The Silent God's Tithe
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior breaks into the guild's sealed vault of tithes owed to Veth and finds nine years of unanswered offerings, plus a contract bearing their own soul-mark. Emotional beat: rage curdling into purpose.

chapters.title: A Dragon-Keeper's Daughter
chapters.summary: Nim's POV. Introduce Nim Ashvael, last keeper of the guttering dragon Emberless, who comes to the guild seeking fuel for a fire that must not go out. Emotional beat: stubborn hope against certain loss.

chapters.title: Terms of Partnership
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior bargains with Nim: guild resources for passage beneath the mountain. Ombre forbids it; Lior resigns from the only family they've known. Emotional beat: severing ties to save oneself.

chapters.title: The Road That Remembers
chapters.summary: Nim's POV. On the mountain road, the landscape replays memories of travelers; Lior's memories surface including ones that aren't theirs—the court's implanted past. Emotional beat: distrust of one's own mind.

chapters.title: Ink and Ash
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa decodes the codex's marginalia: the prophecy's author was the previous soul-seller, and the date marks not Lior's death but the court's centennial collection. Emotional beat: scholarly dread becoming resolve.

chapters.title: The Tollhouse of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The trio pays a toll in memories; Lior sacrifices a memory of Ombre teaching them letters, and grieves it without knowing why. Emotional beat: the cost of moving forward.

chapters.title: Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Nim's POV. First sight of the underground city of glass roots and candle-lit nobility who do not age. Emotional beat: beauty that feels like a trap closing.

chapters.title: A Seat at the Long Table
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The court welcomes Lior as a long-lost asset, offering comfort, wealth, and a chair that fits them perfectly. Emotional beat: temptation of belonging built on lies.

chapters.title: The Soul-Vault
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa infiltrates the archives beneath the throne and finds thousands of soul-jars, each labeled like a ledger line. Emotional beat: cold fury at bureaucratic evil.

chapters.title: Emberless Speaks
chapters.summary: Nim's POV. The dying dragon reveals the truth: her fire doesn't imprison the souls—it keeps the court's hunger contained, and when she dies, the court will feed. Emotional beat: the weight of inherited duty.

chapters.title: Nine Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. In the vault, Lior finds Veth's tithe-jars too—the god didn't go silent; the court stole the god's voice. Emotional beat: grief transformed into solidarity with a wounded god.

chapters.title: The Price of a Chair
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The court offers Lior their soul back freely—if they sign on as the court's new ledger-keeper, replacing the retiring soul-seller. Emotional beat: recognizing the trap dressed as mercy.

chapters.title: Refusal, Notarized
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Lior refuses in writing, and the court's masks slip; the trio flees through glass-root tunnels pursued by polite, tireless servants. Emotional beat: terror sharpened into defiance.

chapters.title: What Ombre Never Told Me
chapters.summary: Ombre's POV. Interlude: the guildmaster races to the mountain with the guild's oldest contracts, revealing she once bought back half of Lior's soul and hid the debt. Emotional beat: guilt seeking redemption.

chapters.title: Half a Soul's Worth of Feeling
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Reunited with Ombre, Lior realizes their emotional numbness was never temperament but theft. Emotional beat: mourning the self they might have been.

chapters.title: The Centennial Collection
chapters.summary: Nim's POV. The court begins gathering souls for the hundred-year feast; Emberless's fire gutters visibly above the city. Emotional beat: countdown pressure.

chapters.title: A Ledger of Debts Owed
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior turns their accounting genius into a weapon: auditing the court's own contracts and finding a clause that voids all sales if the original seller's signature is forged or dead. Emotional beat: hope through precision.

chapters.title: The Forger's Grave
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The trio locates the original soul-seller's tomb inside the mountain; the corpse still holds the signing hand the court preserved. Emotional beat: macabre determination.

chapters.title: Witnessed by Glass
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The court catches them at the tomb; a masked noble reveals herself as the buyer who purchased infant Lior—and as someone who remembers Lior's mother. Emotional beat: longing weaponized.

chapters.title: My Mother's Name
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The noble trades the mother's name for Lior's surrender; Lior almost signs, stopped by Nim's hand on their shoulder. Emotional beat: found family outweighing blood's ghost.

chapters.title: Emberless Falls
chapters.summary: Nim's POV. The dragon's fire fails; the court's containment weakens and hungry nobles begin feeding on the nearest souls—the servants first. Emotional beat: catastrophe and clarity.

chapters.title: Riot of the Unpaid
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The court's servants, learning their wages were their own siphoned life, revolt; chaos becomes cover. Emotional beat: the oppressed finding each other.

chapters.title: The Auditing of Masks
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Amid the riot, Lior publicly reads the court's fraudulent contracts aloud, and each exposed lie cracks a mask. Emotional beat: words as liberation.

chapters.title: Veth Answers
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. With the god's stolen voice-jars shattered in the melee, Veth's presence floods the mountain—and answers Lior's nine years of prayers with a single word: 'Ledger.' Emotional beat: overwhelming grace.

chapters.title: The Last Entry
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Guided by Veth, Lior reaches the master ledger and faces the choice: erase their own sale and keep their power, or destroy the book and free everyone. Emotional beat: the climax of selfhood.

chapters.title: Shatter the Book
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. Lior destroys the master ledger; souls return to bodies across the mountain; the court collapses into ordinary, mortal people. Emotional beat: catharsis.

chapters.title: Ash and Aftermath
chapters.summary: Nim's POV. The trio climbs out into dawn; Emberless, freed from duty, finally rests—but leaves one ember with Nim. Emotional beat: grief and continuation.

chapters.title: The God Who Keeps Accounts
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Veth appears in person: small, tired, an accountant-god who went silent because the court stole the voice, not the faith. Offers Lior a new covenant. Emotional beat: reconciliation without erasure.

chapters.title: Terms Renegotiated
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior negotiates with Veth like a guild contract—no more invisibility, no more unpaid devotion. Emotional beat: agency reclaimed.

chapters.title: Reopening the Ledger
chapters.summary: Ombre's POV. Back at the guild, Ombre offers Lior partnership, not employment; the Gilded Ledger will now trade only in things freely given. Emotional beat: institutional repentance.

chapters.title: Sefa's Catalogue of the Freed
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa begins documenting every freed soul so no one is ever unlabeled again; finds Lior's mother alive in a far port, listed among the returned. Emotional beat: trembling anticipation.

chapters.title: The Woman at the Well Gate
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior travels to meet their mother and discovers she sold them to save them from the court's collectors—a terrible love, finally understood. Emotional beat: forgiveness without pretense.

chapters.title: Dinner with Strangers Who Aren't
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. An awkward, warm meal with the mother who is a stranger; Nim and Sefa wait outside, then are invited in. Emotional beat: found family and birth family merging.

chapters.title: New Entries Only
chapters.summary: Guild ensemble POV. Months later, the reformed Ledger takes its first honest trade: a memory of the mountain, donated willingly, priced at one cup of tea. Emotional beat: quiet repair.

chapters.title: The Prophecy, Amended
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa writes a new codex recording what actually happened, striking the old prophecy's authority; Lior's name appears once—as author of their own ending. Emotional beat: authorship of fate.

chapters.title: Veil and Garden
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Final scene: Lior plants a garden over the collapsed mountain's mouth, veil lifted, ledger balanced, god at their elbow taking notes. Emotional beat: peace earned, not given.
